hikes.title: Alum Rock: Penintencia Creek Trail
hikes.blurb: The Penitencia Creek Trail runs all the way from Berryessa BART into Alum Rock Park, and then up the narrow canyon parallel to the roadway

hikes.title: Angel Island State Park
hikes.blurb: Island hikes of varying lengths with fantastic views of San Francisco and the greater Bay Area, plus historic buildings.

hikes.title: Black Diamond Mines: Clayton to Antioch
hikes.blurb: Isolated valleys, each with their own strong identity, make up Black Diamond Mines, with windswept grassland, woodland, chaparral, and even evergreen forest. Mining history permeates the area.

hikes.title: Coyote Valley: Arrowhead Loop
hikes.blurb: Coyote Valley Open Space Preserve offers views over Morgan Hill from its grassy and oaky shoulder.

hikes.title: Cull Canyon: Along Cull Creek
hikes.blurb: A short, calm hike up a canyon with bay laurels.

hikes.title: Dry Creek Pioneer Regional Park: Pioneer Trail Loop
hikes.blurb: Largely-shaded trails along creeks in classic East Bay rolling hills.

hikes.title: Harvey Ranch to Las Trampas / Moraga to Danville
hikes.blurb: From Moraga to Danville via some of the most remote parts of the East Bay

hikes.title: Marin Headlands: Golden Gate Bridge to Marin City
hikes.blurb: See the Golden Gate Bridge and hike up into the Marin headlands for expansive views of San Francisco, the bridge, and the Bay.

hikes.title: Briones: Walter Costa to Lafayette Ridge loop
hikes.blurb: A steep trek with incredible panoramic views of the inner East Bay, Mt Diablo, and even Mt Tam.

hikes.title: Las Trampas: Ringtail Cat to Ridge to Del Amigo
hikes.blurb: Climb the rocky ridgeline from suburban Danville up into a rugged East Bay classic.

hikes.title: Leona Heights: Laurel to Merritt College
hikes.blurb: An off-the-beaten-path hike through redwoods and a mural-filled former quarry to a local college.

hikes.title: Mission Peak Regional Preserve
hikes.blurb: The famed Mission Peak attracts all sorts to reach its stony peak perched above Fremont. From the top, panoramic views of the Bay and of the Diablo Range await.

hikes.title: Mount Diablo: Mitchell Canyon to Summit
hikes.blurb: Mount Diablo State Park is the crown jewel of the East Bay. On a clear day, from the summit, 40 of California's 58 counties can be seen, from the Golden Gate Bridge to the Sentinel Dome of Yosemite Valley (provided you have good binoculars).

hikes.title: Mount Tamalpais: Pantoll to East Peak
hikes.blurb: An out-and-back hike up a nicely-graded rail trail to the highest peak in Marin with stunning views of the surrounding mountains and the San Francisco skyline.

hikes.title: Point Reyes National Seashore: Alamere Falls
hikes.blurb: Point Reyes National Seashore is famous for this coastal waterfall, one of only two in the state.

hikes.title: Rancho San Antonio: Rhus Ridge
hikes.blurb: Sprawling green hills and shaded canyons just outside Silicon Valley.

hikes.title: Dr. Aurelia Reinhardt Redwood Regional Park
hikes.blurb: Redwood Regional Park offers trails for all levels of skills and abilities, plus a huge selection of recreation options including archery, a pool, a picnic area, and even the NASA Ames Visitor Center! Come enjoy the towering redwood groves that once built Oakland and San Francisco, or hike out to the East Ridge for sweeping views over the Bay.

hikes.title: San Bruno Mountain State & County Park
hikes.blurb: Just outside San Francisco, head up and over the chapparal slopes of San Bruno Mountain and enjoy 360° views of San Francisco, South City, and beyond.

hikes.title: Santa Teresa: Bernal Loop
hikes.blurb: Santa Teresa County Park, on the far southern end of San José, has sweeping, seemingly endless views of the valley.

hikes.title: Dimond Canyon / Sausal Creek to Montclair
hikes.blurb: A short but fun hike up a shady canyon via redwoods, featuring lots of community art.

hikes.title: Siesta Valley & Claremont Canyon: Orinda to Berkeley
hikes.blurb: A trek over the hills via wildflower territory and eucalyptus groves with views of the city, Berkeley, and inland.

hikes.title: Mount Sutro, Twin Peaks, and Glen Canyon
hikes.blurb: A huge bang for your buck hike across San Francisco's urban ridgeline and deep into Glen Canyon.

hikes.title: Sweeney Ridge: Pacifica from Mori Point to Terra Nova
hikes.blurb: A windbeaten ridgeline with panoramic views of the Bay and the ocean from a historic former Nike missile site.

hikes.title: Sweeney Ridge: Skyline College to San Bruno
hikes.blurb: Views over San Francisco's reservoirs and the Pacific Ocean from the top of a scenic ridge

hikes.title: Wildcat Canyon Regional Park
hikes.blurb: Wildflowers and expansive grassy views from right behind Richmond and El Cerrito.

places.title: Channel Islands National Park
places.blurb: Thousands of years of isolation allowed unique plants and animals to evolve on these windswept Southern Californian islands, perfect for exploring over a weekend on foot or by kayak.

places.title: Lake Tahoe
places.blurb: Tahoe, from Washo dáʔaw, simply means lake, and cobalt-blue Lake Tahoe truly is the lake. The largest alpine lake in North America, it attracts visitors from around the world every season of the year for its skiing, hiking, and water sports in a dramatic mountain setting.

places.title: Yosemite National Park
places.blurb: Consistently one of the country's most-visited national parks, Yosemite deserves its fame. Its towering giant sequoias are dwarfed only by its immense granite cliffs and waterfalls. Buses serve the park year-round from Merced; routes to the Mariposa Grove, the Eastern Sierras, and Fresno are seasonal (May to September).
